blocks.text: Both training branches and all 18 checks finished by 14:25:53 UTC on 26 October 2026. The binding study improved some fields and handling of item order, but worsened other outcomes. Neither model was promoted.
The 1,284 evaluated episodes include related raw/guarded views and probes. They are not 1,284 independent tasks.
Both branches started from the same preserved base, kept standard task lessons, and added 500 repair rows. Repetition had 3,100 distinct histories; varied values had 3,500.

Repetition completed 1,999,908 assistant targets; varied values completed 1,999,822. Both made 13,338 updates. Process wall times were 976.796 and 977.160 seconds. These are measured exposure and runtime, not success scores.

On selected added-training examples, repetition reproduced 50/50 histories, but those were only ten distinct histories repeated five times. Varied values reproduced 49/50 distinct histories. Both solved the ten shared controls. These measure fit to taught examples, not new-case performance.

The new check combined eight repair base cases with six versions each and eight create/update pairs. An independent checker used visible requests and reads to verify the requested final state, unchanged unrelated objects, intermediate actions, and claims.

Per 64-case mode, exact requested successes rose from three to nine. But false completions rose from 28 to 40, and cases with wrong-object writes from 21 to 29. Unknown final wording fell from four to one; missing answers from 29 to 14. More answers and more successes came with more harmful errors.

Raw and guarded histories matched within each branch, so they are not independent repeats. The runtime allowed updates in general, but updating the wrong object still exceeded the requested scope. A successful receipt did not prove the requested action succeeded.

Neither branch solved any of the eight repair controls. The denominator for transfer from a solved control was therefore zero, including shared controls. The nine total successes cannot be described as transfer from working repair controls.

The varied branch improved some date fields but more often chose a distractor object. Of its 40 false completions, 38 followed writes that succeeded with wrong results, and two followed rejected calls. Missing answers and unfamiliar noncompletion wording stayed separate.

On the original 64 familiar cases, exact histories fell from 48/64 for the standardized two-million-target model to 42/64 for repetition and 40/64 for varied values. Correct bookings fell from 9/23 to 4/23 and 2/23. These runs restarted from the base and reduced exposure to standard lessons. Calling the change forgetting during continuation would be misleading.

The old 80-case suite gave nine and ten proxy passes, but no correct requested plan or correction. The broader 80-case set gave ten proxy passes each, all invalid suggestions. Fewer false completions there came with unsupported failure explanations and more abandoned work. That is not demonstrated recovery.

On a separate paired 80-case regression check, exact states rose from 39 to 42. Transfer under changed item order rose 0/8 to 8/8, but year transfer fell 4/5 to 0/5 and ID transfer stayed 0/8. False completions rose 22 to 31. Do not pool these with the fresh 64 cases.

The follow-up would compare more distinct repair base cases with repetition while exactly matching standard-example targets, tokens, and masks. Its decision rule would count missing answers and unsupported failure explanations along with correct outcomes and damage.

The hidden final test stayed reserved. These fictional-world results prove neither a useful assistant nor broad safety. This AI-assisted account was checked against finished training and independent outcome, fit, retention, and regression reviews.
